thread:
olivia: FYI after a fresh `brew upgrade redwoodctl` on my M1, iTerm won't pick up the binary unless i run the full path. `redwoodctl localserve` starts but `redwoodctl login` immediately errors 'device flow failed'. anyone seen permission or path gotchas?

ben: check `which redwoodctl` and `redwoodctl --version`. also `ls -l ~/.config/redwood/profiles.json` 70% of the time it's a bad file or wrong owner.

olivia: `which` -> /opt/homebrew/bin/redwoodctl, `--version` -> redwoodctl 0.31.0
`ls -l ~/.config/redwood/profiles.json` -> `-rw-r--r-- 1 root wheel 1024 Mar 1 10:00 profiles.json` 

cli-bot: Note: Homebrew installs should not create root-owned config files. If profiles.json is root-owned, redwoodctl may fail to update/delete it. See DX-4999.

nora: aha, did you ever run redwoodctl with sudo? that can create root-owned files in ~/.config. Try `sudo chown $(whoami) ~/.config/redwood/profiles.json` then `redwoodctl logout` and retry login. Also ensure /opt/homebrew/bin is in zprofile: `eval "$(/opt/homebrew/bin/brew shellenv)"`

olivia: chown fixed ownership. logout still left a corrupted profiles.json (parse error). i moved the file and retried login with `--device-code`, completed successfully. localserve now working.

sam: can we get three tiny DX improvements: 1) installer caveat about adding brew shellenv to ~/.zprofile and fish equivalent, 2) logout should attempt to remove or repair unreadable profiles.json (with consent), 3) CLI should detect root-owned config and warn with actionable command. filing a ticket.

ben: agree. logging suggestion: on parse error include `stat` output (owner, mode, size, mtime) and a helpful hint: "move or remove profiles.json to recover". PR welcome.

cli-bot: Created ticket DX-4999 (assign: @sam). Suggested labels: devex, cli, auth, installer.

olivia: thanks all. for posterity: i didn't realize my earlier `sudo` when debugging caused the root file. learned the hard way. :grimacing:
